user.title: Configure Grenton Interface
user.description: Enter the IP address, port, and PIN from Grenton Object Manager to connect.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Grenton Interface
reconfigure.description: Re-enter the address, port and current PIN to fetch an updated interface. New widgets will be added; existing entities keep their configuration.

naming.title: Names, areas and units
naming.description: By default device names come from widget labels and interface pages become areas. You can now set, page by page, device and entity (friendly) names, device class, unit and precision of sensors. The same settings are available later in Configure → Names, units and precision.

data.customize_names: Customize names, areas, units and precision

page_names.title: Page {step}/{total}: {page}
page_names.description: Widgets: {count}. Empty field = default. Empty area = no area. Precision is the number of decimals shown in HA.

error.invalid_data: Data from the device was missing or malformed.
error.cannot_connect: Unable to connect to the Grenton Object Manager at the given address.

abort.wrong_interface: The fetched interface belongs to a different installation than the one being reconfigured.

entity_list.title: Configure Entities
entity_list.description: Filter by type or search all entities.

configure_sensor_unit.title: Configure {entity_name} - Unit of Measurement
configure_sensor_unit.description: Choose a unit. Without a device class, you can also enter a custom unit.

configure_slider_mode.title: Configure {entity_name} - Display Mode
configure_slider_mode.description: Choose the display mode for the slider.

configure_slider_unit.title: Configure {entity_name} - Unit of Measurement
configure_slider_unit.description: Select the unit of measurement for selected device class.

configure_scene_action.title: Configure {entity_name} - Scene Action
configure_scene_action.description: Choose the call type, then configure its target and arguments.

configure_on_off_state.title: Configure {entity_name} - State (1/3)
configure_on_off_state.description: Choose Switch or Light and configure the attribute or variable that provides the current state. Changing the entity type changes its entity ID; update dashboard and automation references after saving.

configure_on_off_on_action.title: Configure {entity_name} - Turn on (2/3)
configure_on_off_on_action.description: Choose the call type and configure the turn-on target, value or arguments.

configure_on_off_off_action.title: Configure {entity_name} - Turn off (3/3)
configure_on_off_off_action.description: Choose the call type and configure the turn-off target, value or arguments. Saving reloads the integration and applies all three forms.

configure_dimmer_state.title: Configure {entity_name} - Brightness source (1/4)
configure_dimmer_state.description: Choose the brightness source and its native range. Precision is the number of decimal places sent to Grenton.

configure_dimmer_brightness_action.title: Configure {entity_name} - Set brightness (4/4)
configure_dimmer_brightness_action.description: Use $value$ for the brightness in the native range. For Script/Method, put it in a Lua expression argument. Keep other arguments as needed. Saving reloads the integration.

clu_variables.title: Configure {clu_name} variables
clu_variables.description: Add, edit, or remove custom CLU variables exposed in Home Assistant.

clu_variable_remove.title: Remove a CLU variable entity
clu_variable_remove.description: Remove the selected variable from Home Assistant. Its value on the CLU is kept.

configure_clu_variable.title: Configure a CLU variable
configure_clu_variable.description: Enter the variable name exactly as defined in Grenton and select its value type. Boolean variables become switches; other types become sensors.

data_description.read_mode: Polling uses the CLU's configured interval.

configure_value_v2_type.title: Configure {entity_name} - Entity Type
configure_value_v2_type.description: Choose the entity type and read mode.

data_description.read_mode: Temperatures use periodic reads at the interval configured for the CLU.

configure_value_v2_binary.title: Configure {entity_name} - Binary Sensor
configure_value_v2_binary.description: Choose the device class. By default, positive values mean off (closed) and 0 or negative values mean on (open). Enable Invert state to reverse this mapping. Missing or invalid values remain unknown.

data_description.invert_state: Disabled: positive values are off, 0 is on. Enabled: positive values are on, 0 is off. For Door, Window and Opening, on means open and off means closed.

configure_thermostat.title: Configure {entity_name} - Thermostat
configure_thermostat.description: Enable optional cooling, choose the heating/cooling direction independently of manual/schedule mode, and edit the weekly schedule. Saving a schedule preserves power and operating mode.

add_object.title: Add Grenton object
add_object.description: Identifier in CLU->OBJECT format, e.g. CLU221001234->DOU5678 (button: CLU->scriptName, variable: CLU->featureName). UDP works for CLUs in the myGrenton interface and updates instantly; Gate HTTP needs the configured listener and polls periodically. Z-Wave objects (ZWA…) are detected automatically.

data.name: Name
data.variable: User variable/feature instead of object feature (sensors)

gate_settings.title: Gate HTTP
gate_settings.description:
URL of the HA_Integration_Listener, e.g. http://192.168.1.50/HAlistener. Leave empty to disable the Gate.

Webhook for changes pushed by the Gate (after saving with the option enabled): {webhook_url}

data.push: Receive changes from the Gate via webhook

data_description.scan_interval: With the webhook enabled, polling is only a fallback – a longer interval such as 300 s is fine.

entity_names.title: Page {step}/{total}: {page}
entity_names.description: Widgets: {count}. Empty field = default. Empty area = no area. Precision is the number of decimals shown in HA.

import_grenton_objects.title: Import from Grenton Objects
import_grenton_objects.description:
Found {count} objects to import. Each becomes a manual object of this integration. When taking over, the Grenton Objects entries are removed and the new entities get the same entity_id, name, icon, area, aliases and labels – automations and dashboards keep working. The Gate URL is copied if not set yet.

Skipped (variable on the Gate itself or no entity): {skipped}

data.prefer_udp: Use UDP when the CLU is in the myGrenton interface (instant state)
data.take_over: Take over entities (remove Grenton Objects entries, keep entity_id)

restore_lights.title: Restore lights after CLU restart
restore_lights.description: After a CLU restart (e.g. a power failure) lights are set back to how they were just before it – on/off, brightness and colour. A restart is detected by the Uptime sensor resetting; a plain connection loss changes nothing.

data.enabled: Restore lights after a CLU restart

data_description.exclude: These lights are skipped (e.g. outdoor lights driven by a schedule).

abort.no_grenton_objects: No Grenton Objects objects to import.

error.invalid_configuration: Select valid options and enter valid values.
error.cannot_apply_configuration: Could not save the configuration to the CLU. Check the connection and current temperature limits, then retry.
error.cannot_read_configuration: Could not read the current settings from the CLU. Check the connection and reopen configuration.
error.clu_not_in_interface: This CLU is not in the myGrenton interface. Choose the Gate HTTP connection.
error.gate_not_configured: Configure Gate HTTP in the options first.
error.cannot_connect_gate: No response from the Gate HTTP listener at this URL.

set_thermostat_schedule.name: Set thermostat schedule
set_thermostat_schedule.description: Replace the complete weekly thermostat schedule using its configured temperature limits. Preserves power, mode, heating/cooling direction and schedule metadata.

schedule.name: Weekly schedule
schedule.description: All seven lowercase English weekday names, each with time and temperature pairs. Start each day at 00:00; use 15-minute time boundaries and 0.5°C temperature increments.

run_scene.name: Run scene
run_scene.description: Run a Grenton SCENE script, optionally passing a parameter.

parameter.name: Parameter
parameter.description: Optional value passed verbatim into the script call (Lua syntax: "abc" for a string, 42 for a number). Omit this field to use the scene's saved arguments/value. An empty string calls without arguments.

run_script.name: Run script
run_script.description: Run a named Grenton script directly on a discovered CLU.

script.name: Script
script.description: Name of the script on the selected CLU, without parentheses or arguments.

arguments.name: Typed arguments
arguments.description: Positional arguments. Add, edit, remove, or reorder rows. Omit trailing arguments to use the script's defaults; omit this field or use an empty list to call without arguments.

arguments.name: Arguments
arguments.description: Omit trailing arguments to use the script or method defaults.

schedule_hint.name: Assign each day to one section. Each period lasts until the next start time; the last ends at midnight. Temperatures are in °C. Auto preserves the current heating/cooling direction.

schedule_unavailable.name: Wait for the current schedule and temperature limits from the CLU, then reopen configuration.

cooling_unavailable.name: Cooling requires readable and writable thermostat direction bindings.

day_conflict.name: Select at least one day per section, with no day shared between sections.

limits_hint.name: Scheduled temperatures are preserved when the range changes. All targets must fit the new limits; edit the schedule below if needed.
